fields.name: safe
fields.coerce: `data && data.safe`: tested as true or false. A `null` payload also works
fields.description: If truthy, you come back in `woffice` (spawn 0), not at the death point of your map.

responses.name: Moved
responses.when: All checks pass. The server removes `block`, sets HP to the maximum and MP to half, and on a `hardcore` server resets the character (`reset_player`). Then it moves you with `effect: 1`: to `woffice` with `safe`, else to `G.maps[map].on_death`, else to the `on_death` of `main` (`["main", 5]`). A `player` update follows.

responses.name: Success
responses.when: After the move, the party update and a second `player` update (`u+cid`).

fields.name: cevent
fields.description: Tells the official client to fire its `respawn` code event.

rows.when: No character, or your character is not dead (`rip` is falsy).
You died in a map of the Cave of Many Dreams. The server offers a rescue in the cave (`cave_fallen`): a revival room, unless a vote runs.
The respawn wait did not end: `B.rip_time` (12,000 ms) since `player.rip_time`. On the `HARDCORE` and `TEST` servers `B.rip_time` is -1, so there is no wait.

also.when: Success, if you are in a party: each member, you too.
also.summary: `{list, party}`: the names and the state of the party. See the `party_update` entry.

also.when: Success: one after `new_map`, and one more (`u+cid`) before the `game_response`. On a PvP map the second has `s.invincible` (at least 6,000 ms, `invincible_logic`).
Success: clients that saw you at the death point.
also.summary: `{id, reason: "transport", to, s, effect: 1}`. See the `leave` entry for the fields.
